sections.name: File setup, SERIES_COLORS
sections.title: Imports and series colors
sections.what: Brings in the chart drawing parts, the download helper, the date and milestone helpers, and the theme colors used for the lines.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These are the tools needed for the chart and the export.
sections.watch_out: Colors are assigned by position, so the first line always takes the first color and the order of groups matters for appearance.

sections.name: ForecastView (part 1)
sections.title: Reading settings and sorting projects into periods
sections.what: Reads the milestone, period, metric, grouping and year range from the web address. Goes through every project, takes its date for the milestone, places it in a period, and counts the ones that are left out. Decides which groups get their own line and which fold into Other.
sections.why: Likely reason: counting dropped projects instead of guessing their dates keeps the forecast honest.
sections.watch_out: A project whose date cannot be read is counted as unknown and hidden from the chart, so a change in date parsing could move many projects out of view without an error.

sections.name: ForecastView: if
sections.title: Filling gaps and building chart rows
sections.what: Lists every period from the earliest to the latest, including empty ones. Builds one row per period with counts, or with capex totals. In capex mode, a period whose projects lack capex values is left as a gap. Also defines the layout of the CSV export.
sections.why: Likely reason: adding empty periods stops the chart from joining two distant periods into a false trend.
sections.watch_out: Capex gaps are stored as empty values, not zero, so do not replace them with zero when editing this code.

sections.name: ForecastView (part 3)
sections.title: Controls, warnings and the chart
sections.what: Draws the four setting buttons, the year inputs and the CSV button. Shows chips that explain how many projects were left out. Draws the line chart, where clicking a point selects that period. Shows an empty message when nothing matches.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The chips show the reader what was left out, which matches the careful counting in the earlier section.
sections.watch_out: Changing the period setting clears the selected period, but changing the milestone or metric does not, so the drilldown can show zero projects.

sections.name: ForecastView (part 4)
sections.title: Forecast table and project drilldown
sections.what: Draws a table with one row per period showing counts or totals and the project count. Clicking a row selects that period. The side panel lists the projects in the selected period with their milestone date and capex.
sections.why: Likely reason: the table gives exact numbers beside the chart, and the drilldown answers which projects make up a bar.
sections.watch_out: In capex mode, totals use the coverage helper, which may show a total that is based only on the projects with reported values; check the wording when editing.

summary: A line chart and table showing how many projects, or how much capex, reach a chosen milestone in each quarter or year.
purpose: Lets a user see when projects are expected to reach a milestone such as final investment, construction start or completion, and open the list of projects behind any period.
why: Likely reason: counting and reporting the projects that had to be left out keeps the forecast honest rather than guessing missing dates.
how: Reads the milestone, period, metric, grouping and year range from the web address. For each project, takes its date for that milestone, and counts projects with no usable date, year-only dates in quarter mode, and dates outside the year range as left out. Groups the rest into quarter or year periods, keeps the seven largest groups and folds the rest into Other, and fills in empty periods between the first and last. Draws the chart, the table, the drilldown list and the CSV export, which includes the left-out counts.
inputs: The list of projects, the industry name lookup, and web address settings for milestone, period, metric, grouping, and from and to years. The clicked period is kept in memory.
outputs: A line chart, a period table, a list of projects for the selected period, chips that explain what was left out, and a CSV download.
risks: In capex mode, periods with projects but no reported capex show as gaps, not zero, which a reader may misread. Changing the milestone or metric does not clear the selected period, so the drilldown can show zero projects. Only seven groups get their own line, so smaller groups are merged into Other.
debug: If a period looks too low, check the chips above the chart, which count projects left out for missing or year-only dates. If the chart is empty, check the milestone and the year range. If the CSV total does not match the screen, compare the left-out rows at the bottom of the file. If capex gaps look wrong, check that the project capex values are present.
